components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.english: Please wash your hands.
example.fact: 手 forms 手机 'mobile phone' (literally 'hand machine') and marks skilled people: 歌手 'singer', 选手 'athlete'. It is the base of the 扌 radical on many action verbs.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒu bīngbīng liángliáng de.
examples.english: My hands are icy cold.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng jǔshǒu huídá wèntí.
examples.english: Please raise your hand to answer.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.

example.hanzi: 任何人都可以参加这个活动。
example.pinyin: Rènhé rén dōu kěyǐ cānjiā zhège huódòng.
example.english: Anyone can take part in this activity.
example.fact: 任何 pairs naturally with 都 right after its noun (任何人都..., “anyone at all...”) — the same 都-reinforcement pattern seen in 什么都 and 谁都, turning a plain indefinite word into an emphatic “no matter which” statement.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu rènhé wèntí.
examples.english: I don't have any questions.

examples.hanzi: 任何时候你都可以来找我。
examples.pinyin: Rènhé shíhou nǐ dōu kěyǐ lái zhǎo wǒ.
examples.english: You can come find me at any time.

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking, as in 行, 往, 得.
艮 (gèn) is a close sound clue for hěn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 根 gēn, 恨 hèn and 银 yín.
多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".

example.english: There are a lot of flowers in the park.
example.fact: 很多 stacks the intensifier 很 (“very”) directly onto 多 (“many, much”) — and unlike most nouns quantified with a plain number, 多 by itself can't easily stand as a complete predicate of quantity in a simple statement; it almost always needs 很 (or another degree word) in front of it to sound natural, the same pattern that makes bare 好 sound curt next to a fuller 很好.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān chīle hěn duō cài.
examples.english: I ate a lot of food today.

examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén zài páiduì mǎi piào.
examples.english: Many people are lining up to buy tickets.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking and asking, as in 吗, 呢, 问: 哪 is a question word.
那 (nà) gives the same syllable in a different tone; compare 那 "that" and 哪 "which".
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.english: Where did you go?
example.fact: 哪儿 is the Beijing/Mainland colloquial twin of 哪里 (also in this batch) — both mean “where,” but 哪儿 carries the same r-suffixed (儿化) flavor as 这儿/那儿, marking it as the more casual, spoken-register choice next to the neutral 哪里.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎr yě bù xiǎng qù.
examples.english: I don't want to go anywhere.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī fàng zài nǎr le?
examples.english: Where did you put your phone?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
禾 (grain) — crops, as in 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 和 and 秒 second; 种 is seed or to plant.
中 (zhōng) is a close sound clue for zhǒng/zhòng.

example.hanzi: 我从来没见过这种颜色。
example.pinyin: Wǒ cónglái méi jiànguo zhèzhǒng yánsè.
example.english: I've never seen this kind of color before.
example.fact: 种 is Mandarin's default measure word for categories or types (“kind, sort”), not for physical objects — 这种 pairs the near-demonstrative 这 directly with that classifier the same way 一种, 那种, and 哪种 do, forming a small family of “type-of” phrases built on the same counter.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yě xǐhuan zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: I like this kind of fruit too.

examples.hanzi: 这种天气最适合出去玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng tiānqì zuì shìhé chūqù wán.
examples.english: This kind of weather is best for going out to play.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
帝 (dì) is a sound clue for 蒂 dì (stem base) and 啼 tí; the old shape is possibly a flower calyx, uncertain.

example.hanzi: 很多人相信上帝的存在。
example.pinyin: Hěnduō rén xiāngxìn Shàngdì de cúnzài.
example.english: Many people believe in the existence of God.
example.fact: 上帝 combines 上 (“above, supreme”) with 帝 (“emperor” — originally the ruler who presided over ancestral sacrifice) into “the supreme ruler,” the term Chinese Bible translators adopted for the Christian and Judaic “God,” reusing a title that in ancient texts had also named the highest ancestral deity of the Shang dynasty.

examples.pinyin: Shàngdì a, zhè yě tài nán le!
examples.english: Oh God, this is too hard!

examples.hanzi: 她每天晚上向上帝祈祷。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang xiàng shàngdì qídǎo.
examples.english: She prays to God every night.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Nàge nǚrén shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
example.english: That woman is my teacher.
example.fact: 女人 names a woman in a generic, sometimes slightly blunt way (“a woman,” as opposed to a man), while the more formal, now near-universal polite term for addressing or referring respectfully to a woman is 女士 — swapping one for the other can noticeably shift a sentence's register.

examples.hanzi: 那个女人手里拿着一把伞。
examples.pinyin: Nàge nǚrén shǒu lǐ názhe yì bǎ sǎn.
examples.english: That woman is holding an umbrella.

examples.pinyin: Zhège nǚrén hěn huì zuòfàn.
examples.english: This woman is very good at cooking.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
子 (child) — a child in a house: to bear and nurture; characters were later "born" from other characters.

example.english: What's your name?
example.fact: 名, per its own etymology, pictures calling out with the mouth (口) in the dark of night (夕) — a reminder that a name's oldest job was simply making yourself identifiable when you couldn't be seen. 字 adds the sense of a fixed, written-down designation, so together 名字 reads as “the name, spoken and set down.”

examples.hanzi: 请在这里写下你的名字。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ xiěxià nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please write your name here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàngle tā de míngzi.
examples.english: I forgot his name.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; knowing means being able to name.
只 (zhǐ) is a loose sound clue for shí; the part replaces 戠 in the traditional 識.

example.english: We got to know each other last year.
example.fact: This deck's pilot batch already flagged the 知道/认识 distinction at rank 3: 知道 covers knowing a fact, while 认识 — this word — is needed for knowing a person or place. 认识 has a further sense with no single-word English equivalent: recognizing a written character on sight, as in 你认识这个字吗? (“do you recognize this character?”).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi nàge rén ma?
examples.english: Do you know that person?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú rènshi zhège zì.
examples.english: I don't recognize this character.

components.note: 土 (earth) — two people 从 sitting on the ground 土: to sit. Also in 座 zuò seat.

example.english: Please sit here.
example.fact: 坐 is also 'ride/take' for transport you sit inside: 坐地铁, 坐飞机. For bikes you 'straddle' (骑), and for driving you use 开. 请坐 is the polite 'please sit down'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò dìtiě qù ba.
examples.english: Let's take the subway.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zuò, bié kèqi.
examples.english: Please sit down, make yourself at home.

components.note: 今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.

example.english: Let's eat together tonight.
example.fact: 今晚 belongs to a tidy family of “今 + time-of-day” words — 今天 (today), 今早 (this morning), 今晚 (tonight) — all built by prefixing 今 (“this, now”) directly onto a time-of-day noun, with no preposition needed the way English needs “this.”

examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ yào zài jiā kàn diànyǐng.
examples.english: Tonight I'm going to watch a movie at home.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīnwǎn yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: Are you free tonight?

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 做 do; 他 is "he" (or other).
也 (yě) is only a loose sound hint for tā; the sibling 她 tā (she) shares it with 女 for woman.

example.hanzi: 除了英语,他还会说其他语言。
example.pinyin: Chúle Yīngyǔ, tā hái huì shuō qítā yǔyán.
example.english: Besides English, he can also speak other languages.
example.fact: 其他 and its near-twin 其它 are written with different second characters (他 “he/other person” vs 它 “it, inanimate other”) but pronounced identically and used interchangeably in practice — mainland style guides now generally recommend 其他 for both people and things, letting the once-meaningful distinction fade.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ wèn qítā tóngxué.
examples.english: You can ask the other classmates.

examples.pinyin: Qítā rén dōu huí jiā le.
examples.english: Everyone else went home.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — drinking and speaking: 吃, 吸, 呼; 喝 is to drink.
曷 (hé) sounds exactly like 喝; also in 渴 kě thirsty and 歇 xiē.

example.english: What would you like to drink?
example.fact: 喝 covers drinks and soup: 喝汤 'have soup' (literally 'drink soup'). Medicine is usually 吃药 but Chinese medicine soup is 喝. In 喝彩 'cheer', the same character is read hè.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang xǐhuan hē niúnǎi.
examples.english: I like to drink milk in the morning.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù hē bēi kāfēi ba.
examples.english: Let's go have a cup of coffee.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bú jìde tā de míngzi le.
example.english: I don't remember his name anymore.
example.fact: 记得 is negated with 不 rather than 没 (不记得, never 没记得) even though it describes a memory state rather than a discrete action — a reminder that 没 generally negates completed events or existence, while 不 negates ongoing states, habits, and abilities.

examples.hanzi: 你记得我的电话号码吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jìde wǒ de diànhuà hàomǎ ma?
examples.english: Do you remember my phone number?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jìde tā shì qùnián lái de.
examples.english: I remember he came last year.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.english: This guy is always late.
example.fact: 家伙 literally started out meaning “household gear” — pots, tools, furniture, even livestock, anything kept “at home” (家) as a working “companion” (伙), senses still listed in its dictionary entry — before it drifted into today's dominant colloquial sense, a casual, often faintly disrespectful “guy” or “fellow.”

examples.pinyin: Nàge jiāhuo shì shéi?
examples.english: Who is that guy?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhège xiǎo jiāhuo zhēn kě'ài!
examples.english: You little rascal, you're so cute!

components.note: The shape does not explain 与 today (simplified from 與, two hands handing something over). Memory aid: a hand passing a thing along, hence 'give' and then 'and, with'.

example.pinyin: Tā yǔ péngyou yìqǐ qù lǚxíng.
example.english: He went travelling with friends.
example.fact: 与 is a more formal 'and/with' than 和, common in titles and writing: 战争与和平 'War and Peace'. It also appears in 参与 'participate' and 与其…不如… 'rather than…'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǔ tā shì tóngxué.
examples.english: He and I are classmates.

examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng yǔ kuàilè zuì zhòngyào.
examples.english: Health and happiness matter the most.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — a weapon guarding a place 口: 或 first meant a defended territory (域 yù adds 土). "Perhaps, or" is a later use.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 你可以喝茶,或者喝咖啡。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ hē chá, huòzhě hē kāfēi.
example.english: You can drink tea, or drink coffee.
example.fact: 或者 connects statements — a genuine choice being offered or described (“A or B”) — while its close relative 还是 is reserved for actual yes/no questions (“A or B?”); mixing the two up is one of the most common structural slips intermediate learners make.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan chá huòzhě kāfēi?
examples.english: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.hanzi: 你可以今天来,或者明天来。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ jīntiān lái, huòzhě míngtiān lái.
examples.english: You can come today, or come tomorrow.

components.note: 写 (xiě) — to write; as a part it sounds out 泻 xiè (to flow out).

example.hanzi: 请把你的名字写在这里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de míngzi xiě zài zhèlǐ.
example.english: Please write your name here.
example.fact: 写 covers writing characters (写字), composing (写文章 'write an essay') and describing. It differs from 画 'draw'. Its traditional form 寫 is much more complex.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài gěi péngyou xiě yì fēng xìn.
examples.english: He is writing a letter to a friend.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xiě rìjì.
examples.english: I write in my diary every day.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 is a hole, as in 空, 窗, 突; 穿 is to pierce through, and the 牙 is a tooth boring in.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
example.english: It's cold today, so wear more clothes.
example.fact: 穿 is used for clothes, shoes and socks, but hats, glasses and jewellery take 戴. Its original meaning is 'to pierce', which remains in 穿过 'pass through' and 看穿 'see through'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ chuān zhè jiàn yīfu hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: You look good wearing this dress.

examples.pinyin: Háizi chuān bu shàng zhè shuāng xié le.
examples.english: The child can't fit into these shoes anymore.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — playing with a piece of jade; also in 国 country, 宝 treasure.
廾 (two hands) — hands holding something; 弄 is to handle or play with.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shǒujī nòng huài le.
example.english: I broke my phone.
example.fact: 弄 is a colloquial all-purpose verb that stresses the outcome: 弄坏 'break', 弄丢 'lose', 弄清楚 'make clear'. Read lòng it means 'alley', as in the Shanghai-style 弄堂.

examples.pinyin: Bié nònghuài wǒ de shǒujī.
examples.english: Don't break my phone.

examples.hanzi: 我来弄午饭，你休息一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái nòng wǔfàn, nǐ xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: I'll make lunch, you take a rest.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.pinyin: Guòqù, zhèlǐ shì yí piàn nóngtián.
example.english: In the past, this used to be farmland.
example.fact: 过去 does triple duty: a noun for “the past” (在过去, “in the past”), a verb meaning “to pass by, go over” (走过去, “walk over there”), and, attached after another verb, a directional complement meaning motion away from the speaker (拿过去, “take it over there”) — three grammatical roles riding on the same two characters.

examples.pinyin: Shíjiān guòqù de zhēn kuài.
examples.english: Time passes so fast.

examples.pinyin: Tā zǒu guòqù dǎkāile mén.
examples.english: He walked over and opened the door.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking and asking, as in 吗, 呢, 问: 哪 is a question word.
那 (nà) gives the same syllable in a different tone; compare 那 "that" and 哪 "which".
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.english: Where's your bag?
example.fact: Said twice in a row as a stock reply — “哪里哪里” — 哪里 turns into an almost automatic way to deflect a compliment (“oh, not at all,” literally “where, where?”) rather than asking a real question, a politeness convention with no literal English equivalent.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng qù nǎlǐ wán?
examples.english: Where do you want to go to have fun?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎlǐ dōu bù xiǎng qù.
examples.english: I don't want to go anywhere.

meanings: particle: 了 + 啊, lively statement

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech and spoken particles, as in 吗, 呢, 吧; 啦 is a lively final particle.
拉 (lā) gives the sound exactly: 啦 lā.

example.english: We're here!
example.fact: 啦 is a fusion of 了 and 啊 and gives a bright, informal tone: 好啦 'OK, OK', 吃饭啦 'dinner's ready!'. It appears in speech and chat, and is rare in formal writing.

examples.pinyin: Xiàbān la, wǒmen huí jiā ba!
examples.english: Work is over, let's go home!

examples.pinyin: Bié kū la, méi guānxi de.
examples.english: Stop crying, it's okay.

components.note: 去 (qù) — close sound: 却 què. The 卩 on the right was once a kneeling person; 却 means retreat, then but.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, què bù xiǎng xiūxi.
example.english: He is tired, but he doesn't want to rest.
example.fact: 却 goes after the subject and before the verb: 我想去，他却不想. It signals unexpected contrast and is often paired with 但是 or 可是: 他很聪明，但是却不努力. Unlike 但, it never starts a clause.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu hěn duō qián, què bú kuàilè.
examples.english: He has a lot of money, yet he isn't happy.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bāng tā, tā què bù jiēshòu.
examples.english: I wanted to help him, but he didn't accept it.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.

example.pinyin: Qǐng suàn yíxià zǒnggòng duōshao qián.
example.english: Please work out how much it is in total.
example.fact: 算 means 'to calculate', and by extension 'to count as': 这也算好吃 'this counts as tasty'. 算了 'forget it' and 打算 'plan to' are very common, as is 算数 'to count (as valid)'.

examples.hanzi: 我们算一下一共多少人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen suàn yíxià yígòng duōshao rén.
examples.english: Let's count how many people there are in all.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng yě suàn búcuò le.
examples.english: This counts as pretty good, too.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱; 担 is to carry on the shoulder, then to bear a duty.
旦 (dàn) is a close sound clue for dān; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 胆 dǎn.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, yíqiè dōu huì hǎo de.
example.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
example.fact: 担 on its own means “to carry, to shoulder” (as in carrying a load on a shoulder pole) — 担心 pictures worry as a weight literally shouldered on the 心 (“heart, mind”), the same image English draws on with “a load off my mind” or “carrying a worry.”

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn dānxīn nǐ de shēntǐ.
examples.english: I'm very worried about your health.

examples.pinyin: Māma dānxīn háizi huì gǎnmào.
examples.english: Mom worries the child will catch a cold.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and connections, as in 红, 给, 经, 系; 继 is to keep a thread going.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and connections, as in 红, 给, 经, 继; a thread that goes on.
卖 stands in for 賣 in 續, only a loose sound clue for xù.

example.english: Please everyone continue working.
example.fact: 继 and 续 are near-synonyms doubled into one word — both independently mean “to continue, to carry on an unbroken thread,” continuing the same 纟 (“thread”) imagery visible in both characters' own components — the same reinforcement strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该, elsewhere in this deck.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng jìxù shuō, wǒ zài tīng.
examples.english: Please go on, I'm listening.

examples.hanzi: 他想继续在这家公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng jìxù zài zhè jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: He wants to keep working at this company.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 迷; 送 is walking someone off, or delivering.

example.english: I'll take you home.
example.fact: 送 covers gifts (送礼物), deliveries (送货) and escorting: 送你回家 'see you home', 送行 'see someone off'. 送给 marks the recipient: 送给她一朵花.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng sòng māma yí jiàn lǐwù.
examples.english: I want to give my mom a gift.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng sòng wǒ, wǒ zìjǐ zǒu.
examples.english: You don't need to see me off, I'll walk myself.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.

example.hanzi: 那个女孩在公园里跳舞。
example.pinyin: Nàge nǚhái zài gōngyuán lǐ tiàowǔ.
example.english: That girl is dancing in the park.
example.fact: 女孩 is the casual, everyday counterpart to the more formal or bookish 女孩子 and 姑娘 — in spoken Mandarin, 女孩(儿) is usually the default choice for “girl,” with an optional 儿-suffix common in Beijing-area speech.

examples.pinyin: Zhège nǚhái jīnnián wǔ suì.
examples.english: This girl is five this year.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge ài xiào de nǚhái.
examples.english: She's a girl who loves to laugh.

meanings: (in 以前, 以后) before, after

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.

example.english: Let's talk about it later.
example.fact: 以 is a formal 'by/using' that survives in set words: 可以 'may', 所以 'therefore', 以前 'before', 以后 'after', 以为 'to assume'. In writing it forms 以…为… 'take… as…'.

examples.pinyin: Yǐqián wǒ zhù zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: I used to live in Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng wǒ de diànnǎo.
examples.english: You can use my computer.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.english: The children are playing in the park.
example.fact: 玩 is 'play for fun', not sport (that's 打球) and not instruments (弹钢琴). 玩手机 'mess about on the phone', 好玩 'fun', 玩笑 'joke'. 玩儿 is the Beijing form.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò nǐ xiǎng qù nǎr wán?
examples.english: Where do you want to go for fun this weekend?

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan wán diànnǎo yóuxì.
examples.english: He likes playing computer games.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.

example.english: Darling, you're back!
example.fact: 亲爱 almost never stands alone as a plain adjective — it shows up overwhelmingly in the fixed form 亲爱的, used both as a term of endearment addressing someone directly and, in more formal writing, as the salutation opening a letter (“Dear ___”).

examples.pinyin: Qīn'ài de péngyou, nǐ hǎo!
examples.english: Dear friend, hello!

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì qīn'ài de jiārén.
examples.english: He is my dearest family.

meanings: (indicates continuation from the past towards us)

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.english: He slowly sat down.
example.fact: 下来 is one of Mandarin's most productive direction-plus-result suffixes: literally “down + come,” it attaches after action verbs to mark downward movement toward the speaker (坐下来, “sit down”) but also extends abstractly to mark a state settling into place (安静下来, “to quiet down”) — a single suffix spanning both the literal and the metaphorical.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ bǎ jiàgé jiàng xiàlai.
examples.english: Please bring the price down.

examples.hanzi: 天黑了,车子慢慢停了下来。
examples.pinyin: Tiān hēi le, chēzi mànmān tíngle xiàlai.
examples.english: It got dark, and the car slowly came to a stop.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.english: We became good friends.
example.fact: 成 means 'become' (成为) and 'succeed': 成功 'success', 成绩 'results/grades'. As a result ending it means 'turn into': 变成 'become'. Northern speech uses 成 as 'OK': 成！ 'Fine!'

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chéngwéi yì míng yīshēng.
examples.english: He wants to become a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 这件事成了，我们很高兴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì chéng le, wǒmen hěn gāoxìng.
examples.english: The deal worked out, and we're very happy.

meanings: measure word for long thin things

components.note: 木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.

example.english: This road is very long.
example.fact: 条 counts long, thin or flexible things: 路, 河, 鱼, 裤子 'trousers', 狗 'dog', 蛇 'snake'. It also means 'article/clause': 条件 'condition', 条约 'treaty'. Simplified from 條.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile yì tiáo kùzi.
examples.english: I bought a pair of pants.

examples.hanzi: 那条河又宽又长，很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Nà tiáo hé yòu kuān yòu cháng, hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: That river is wide and long, and very pretty.

components.note: 句 (jù, sentence) is a close sound clue for gòu; also in 构 gòu, 沟 gōu and 钩 gōu.
多 (many) — meaning "more than enough".

example.english: Is the money enough?
example.fact: 够 means 'enough': 不够 'not enough', 够了！ 'That's enough!' Before an adjective it adds 'quite' (够大) and in the sense 'to reach' it needs ability: 够不着 'can't reach'.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi gòu le.
examples.english: This is enough stuff.

examples.hanzi: 我的钱不够，你有零钱吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de qián bú gòu, nǐ yǒu língqián ma?
examples.english: I don't have enough money, do you have change?

components.note: 父 (father) — a hand holding a stone axe, an image of the household head who works and rules.
亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.

example.pinyin: Wǒ fùqīn shì yì míng yīshēng.
example.english: My father is a doctor.
example.fact: 父亲 is the formal, written-register word for “father” — built from 父 (traditionally read as a hand gripping a tool, evoking a father wielding it to provide for the family) plus 亲 (“close kin”) — while everyday spoken Mandarin overwhelmingly prefers the more casual 爸爸 when addressing or talking about one's own dad.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ fùqīn měitiān zǎoshang pǎobù.
examples.english: My father jogs every morning.

examples.hanzi: 父亲节我给他买了一件礼物。
examples.pinyin: Fùqīn Jié wǒ gěi tā mǎile yí jiàn lǐwù.
examples.english: I bought him a gift for Father's Day.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.english: I used to live in Shanghai.
example.fact: 以前 and 之前 (rank 104, also in this batch) are near-synonyms for “before,” but 以前 more often stands alone as a free-floating time word (“in the past, before now”), while 之前 more typically attaches directly after a specific clause or noun (X之前, “before X”) — a subtle distributional difference two words that translate the same in English don't reveal.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǐqián shì wǒ de tóngxué.
examples.english: He used to be my classmate.

examples.hanzi: 三年以前,我们见过一次。
examples.pinyin: Sān nián yǐqián, wǒmen jiànguo yí cì.
examples.english: We met once three years ago.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 足 (⻊ on the left) is the foot radical, as in 跳 jump, 路 road, 踢 kick; 跑 is to run.
包 (bāo) — near sound — 跑 is pǎo; 包 also sounds out 抱 bào, 饱 bǎo and 泡 pào.

example.english: He runs very fast.
example.fact: 跑 is 'run' (in classical Chinese 走 meant 'run'). 跑步 is 'jogging/running', 跑腿 'run errands'. It can also mean 'flee' or 'leak': 车跑了 'the car left'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù pǎobù ba.
examples.english: Let's go jogging together.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu pǎojìnle fángjiān.
examples.english: The puppy ran into the room.

components.note: 月 — a crescent moon, also the word for month; in body words ⺼ is a different part, as in 脸 face.

example.english: January has thirty-one days.
example.fact: 月 is both 'moon' and 'month'. Months are simply numbers + 月: 一月 to 十二月, and 月份 means 'month' in the calendar sense. The same shape also appears in body-part characters (as a form of 肉 'flesh').

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jǐ yuè chūshēng?
examples.english: Which month were you born?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià ge yuè qù Běijīng.
examples.english: I'm going to Beijing next month.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.english: He moved to the US last year.
example.fact: A common explanation for 美国 is that it's a phonetic-plus-flattering transliteration of “America” — 美 was chosen partly for its sound (Měi echoing “Ame-”) and partly because 美 independently means “beautiful,” following the same pattern used to coin other country names, as in 英国 (“hero-nation,” England) and 德国 (“virtue-nation,” Germany).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Měiguó xuéxí.
examples.english: I want to study in the United States.

examples.pinyin: Měiguó de dōngtiān hěn lěng ma?
examples.english: Is winter in the United States very cold?

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.

example.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān qǐ de hěn zǎo.
example.english: You got up very early today.
example.fact: 早 stands alone as 'Good morning!' (早！) and builds 早上 'morning', 早饭 'breakfast'. It can mean 'long ago': 我早就知道了 'I knew it long ago'. Its opposite is 晚.

examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang hǎo, nǐ chī zǎofàn le ma?
examples.english: Good morning, have you had breakfast?

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yào zǎodiǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.english: Tomorrow I need to get up early.

components.note: 长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.english: Her hair is very long.
example.fact: 长 is read cháng for 'long' but zhǎng for 'grow' or 'chief': 长大 'grow up', 校长 'school principal', 长辈 'elders'. So the same character covers both 'long' and 'elder' in one old picture of long-haired age.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo mǎlù hěn cháng.
examples.english: This road is very long.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa bǐ wǒ de cháng.
examples.english: His hair is longer than mine.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wánquán tóngyì nǐ de kànfǎ.
example.english: I completely agree with your view.
example.fact: 完全 works as both an adjective (“complete, whole”) describing a noun and an adverb (“completely, totally”) modifying a verb or adjective without changing form at all — placement in the sentence, not any suffix, is what signals which role it's playing.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ wánquán bù zhīdào.
examples.english: I had no idea about this at all.

examples.hanzi: 房间已经完全准备好了。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān yǐjīng wánquán zhǔnbèi hǎo le.
examples.english: The room is completely ready.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).
贝 (cowrie) — a shell, once used as money. As a radical it marks money and value: 财 wealth, 货 goods, 买 buy, 费 cost.

example.hanzi: 这幅画是他最珍贵的宝贝。
example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà shì tā zuì zhēnguì de bǎobèi.
example.english: This painting is his most treasured possession.
example.fact: 贝 is a pictograph of a cowrie shell, once used as currency in ancient China — 宝贝 layers a second “treasure” character (宝, valuables kept under a roof) directly on top of it, so the word for a literal treasured object doubles as Mandarin's most common affectionate term for a baby or loved one, much like English “treasure” or “precious.”

examples.pinyin: Bǎobèi, gāi qǐchuáng le!
examples.english: Sweetie, time to get up!

examples.hanzi: 妈妈抱着她的宝贝睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Māma bàozhe tā de bǎobèi shuìzháo le.
examples.english: Mom fell asleep holding her baby.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.

example.english: Today is the 3rd.
example.fact: 号 gives the day of the month in speech: 三号 'the 3rd' (written 日). It also means 'number' (号码, 房间号) and 'size' (大号 'large'). Read háo it means 'to wail'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fángjiān hàomǎ shì duōshao?
examples.english: What is your room number?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ shì duōshao?
examples.english: What is your phone number?

components.note: 木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.

example.english: The police officer has a gun.
example.fact: 枪 originally meant 'spear' and now mostly means 'gun': 手枪 'pistol', 开枪 'fire a gun'. Its measure word is 把 or 支. In 红缨枪 it still means a spear.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的人拿着一把枪。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de rén názhe yì bǎ qiāng.
examples.english: The man in the movie is holding a gun.

examples.pinyin: Wánjù qiāng shì háizi de lǐwù.
examples.english: The toy gun is a present for the child.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — marks animals, as in 猫 cat, 猪 pig, 猴 monkey; 狗 is a dog.
句 (jù) is a loose hint for gǒu; 够 gòu and 钩 gōu share it.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì tiáo gǒu.
example.english: We have a dog at home.
example.fact: 狗 takes the measure word 条 or 只: 一条狗, 一只小狗. It's one of the twelve zodiac animals (属狗 'born in the Year of the Dog'). The word appears in many idioms; some are insults, so 狗 isn't always friendly.

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān dài gǒu qù sànbù.
examples.english: He takes his dog for a walk every day.

examples.pinyin: Nà zhī xiǎogǒu zhēn kě'ài.
examples.english: That little dog is so cute.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 我很想去,可是没有时间。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎng qù, kěshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
example.english: I really want to go, but I don't have time.
example.fact: 可是 was already flagged at rank 18 of this deck's pilot batch (但是) as sitting a shade more conversational than the neutral 但是 — of Mandarin's three common “but” words, 可是 leans spoken and slightly emphatic, 但是 is the neutral default, and 不过 is the softest, most casual of the three.

examples.hanzi: 这个很便宜,可是不太好用。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hěn piányi, kěshì bú tài hǎoyòng.
examples.english: This is cheap, but it's not very useful.

examples.hanzi: 他可是我们班最高的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā kěshì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de rén.
examples.english: He is indeed the tallest in our class.

components.note: 世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.
田 (field) — fields have boundaries, which is what 界 means.
介 (jiè) gives the exact sound; 介 also sounds out 价 jià.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù kànkan zhège shìjiè.
example.english: I want to go see the world.
example.fact: 世, per its own character-card etymology, depicts three leaves or shoots stacked on a stem — a picture of successive generations growing one atop another — and 界 separately contributes “boundary” (from 田, the line between fields); 世界 literally reads as “the bounded span of generations,” an unexpectedly poetic origin for today's plain word “world.”

examples.pinyin: Shìjiè shàng yǒu hěn duō guójiā.
examples.english: There are many countries in the world.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì shìjiè yǒumíng de gēshǒu.
examples.english: He is a world-famous singer.
